features.what: The heroes the simulator's test fights and the measured threat use: the seven SRD pregens at levels 1-20 with every SRD level benefit, plus a Bard, a Sorcerer and a Monk (Ren, levels 1-20 since 28 October: Disciplined Survivor, Perfect Focus, Superior Defense and Body and Mind played). Levels 10-20 come from the character builder (no errors, nothing left to choose): Ability Score Improvements, Epic Boons at 19, capstones at 20 (Hero 5's Primal Champion, Hero 1's Three Extra Attacks), spells up to level 9, Mystic Arcanum. Played: Tactical Master (Push, Sap or Slow on Hero 1's attack), Studied Attacks, Heroic Rally, Supreme Sneak's Stealth Attack, Improved Cunning Strike, Relentless Rage, Improved Brutal Strike, Abjure Foes, Aura of Courage, Radiant Strikes, Aura Expansion, Empowered Evocation, Supreme Healing, Slippery Mind. Since 27 October also Elusive, Indomitable Might, Persistent Rage, Remarkable Athlete (Initiative and Athletics) and Blessed Strikes on Play live's cantrips with Improved Blessed Strikes' Temporary Hit Points. Fiendish Resilience: the player picks the damage type in the rest dialog as a Short or Long Rest ends; the Warlock has Resistance to it in the next fights. Since 28 October the Sorcerer Hero 10 goes to level 20 too (Draconic Sorcery; Metamagic at 10 and 17, spells up to level 9, Boon of Spell Recall at 19): Dragon Wings (14) is a button with her class features, a Bonus Action that gives her a Fly Speed of 60 ft for the fight, once per Long Rest or for 3 Sorcery Points, and she can dismiss them at any time; Arcane Apotheosis (20) makes one Metamagic option free on each of her turns while Innate Sorcery is active, the costliest one she picks (her Sorcery line on the sheet says when it is free). Since 28 October the Bard, Hero 9, goes to level 20 too (College of Lore, from the character builder; at level 5 she is the Hero 9 you know): Ability Score Improvements, the Boon of Spell Recall at 19, Magical Discoveries (Fireball, Counterspell) and Magical Secrets (Cone of Cold, Chain Lightning, Meteor Swarm, Heal, Mass Heal), spells up to level 9. Played: Superior Inspiration (18: when a fight starts she has at least two Bardic Inspiration uses) and Words of Creation (20: Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill always prepared, and each can take a second creature within 10 feet of the first). Since 28 October the casters' high-level features play in a fight too. Hero 4 (Evoker): Overchannel (14) is a question when she casts a Wizard damage spell with a level 1-5 slot (Fireball, Cone of Cold, Magic Missile, Scorching Ray, Shatter, Web, Wall of Fire): say yes and its damage dice roll their highest that turn; the first use after a Long Rest is free, each later one costs her 2d12 Necrotic per slot level (1d12 more each time again), which nothing resists. Spell Mastery (18) casts Magic Missile and Scorching Ray at their lowest level with no slot, as often as she likes; Signature Spells (20) casts Fireball and Counterspell once each with no slot until a Short or Long Rest. Spell Mastery's spells must take an action to cast (SRD 5.2.1), so Hero 4's are now Magic Missile and Scorching Ray instead of Shield and Misty Step (she keeps those two prepared). Vex (Fiend): Hurl Through Hell (14) on a hit with an attack roll, once per turn: a Charisma save or 8d10 Psychic (none for a Fiend) and the creature is gone until the end of his next turn (nobody can target it and it loses its turns), then it comes back to its space; once per Long Rest, or a Pact Magic slot gives the use back. Eldritch Master (20): Magical Cunning, a button on his card on the adventure page (a 1-minute rite, once per Long Rest), gives back all his Pact Magic slots instead of half. Hero 2: Divine Intervention (10) is a question on the Cast card of each Cleric spell of level 1-5 the table casts (Bless, Guiding Bolt, Healing Word, Cure Wounds, Shield of Faith, Spiritual Weapon, Spirit Guardians, Command, Aid, Dispel Magic, Revivify, Banishment, Flame Strike, Mass Healing Word, Mass Cure Wounds): a Magic action, no slot, no Material components (Revivify's diamond too), once per Long Rest. Any other Cleric spell of level 5 or lower: Ask the GM's Divine Intervention, which now takes her Magic action and the same use. Greater Divine Intervention (20): Wish through Ask the GM; after it, no Divine Intervention until 2d4 Long Rests are done (the adventure day counts them). The computer-played heroes use them too: Hero 4's free Overchannel on a Fireball or Cone of Cold, her Signature Fireball and her Spell Mastery Magic Missile and Scorching Ray with no slot; Vex hurls a foe with more than 20 Hit Points while his free use is left; Hero 2 casts Mass Cure Wounds by Divine Intervention when no level 5 slot is left and allies are down. Since 28 October the Fighter, Thief, Berserker and Devotion Paladin features that went to the GM are played too (Hero 1, Hero 3, Hero 5, Hero 6, or any character the builder makes with them): Tactical Mind (a failed Hide, Study or Influence check gets +1d10 for a Second Wind use, kept if the check still fails), Tactical Shift (Second Wind also gives half the Speed of movement that provokes no Opportunity Attacks), Heroic Warrior (Heroic Inspiration at the start of each turn; it rerolls a missed attack roll, a failed save or a failed check), Devious Strikes (Daze, Knock Out or Obscure on a Sneak Attack), Thief's Reflexes (a second turn in the first round, at Initiative minus 10), Stroke of Luck (a failed attack roll, save or check becomes a 20, once per Short or Long Rest), Retaliation (a melee attack back, the Reaction, when a creature within 5 feet damages the Berserker), Intimidating Presence (a Bonus Action: a Wisdom save or Frightened for 1 minute, saving again each turn; once per Long Rest or for a use of Rage), Restoring Touch (Lay On Hands ends Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed or Stunned, 5 points of the pool each), Smite of Protection (after a Divine Smite, the Paladin and her allies in her aura have Half Cover until her next turn) and Holy Nimbus (a Bonus Action: an enemy starting its turn in her aura takes Radiant damage, she has Advantage on saves Fiends and Undead force, and the aura is sunlight; once per Long Rest or for a level 5 slot). The computer-played heroes use them too. Since 28 October (GM: "I don't want any of the test characters. I only want to use characters saved in the saved characters tab"): the pages no longer offer them; they stay inside Mythastria for its own checks and the measured threat Remix reads.
features.how: Not offered on the pages since 28 October; Mythastria's own checks still use them.
features.limits: Asked of the GM (Ask the GM in Play live): Use Magic Device (no charged items or Spell Scrolls in a fight). Spells of levels 4-9 the table can't cast yet go to the GM too; Mystic Arcanum spells need no slot there. Slow and Abjure Foes do not yet change how far creatures move. Hero 10's Dragon Companion (18) is asked of the GM (Summon Dragon is a summoned creature, still the GM's); a computer-played Hero 10 does not call up her wings. Hero 9's Countercharm, Peerless Skill, Jack of All Trades, Counterspell, Hold Person, Hold Monster, Dispel Magic, Foresight and her other utility spells are asked of the GM; Cutting Words is asked live as before. Overchannel needs a spell slot, so it is not offered on a Spell Mastery or Signature Spells cast with no slot; spells that keep hurting on later turns (Web, Wall of Fire) are at their highest only on the turn cast. A creature hurled through Hell keeps its token on the map while it is gone. Divine Intervention for a spell the table doesn't cast, and Wish, are ruled by the GM; Magical Cunning in the middle of a fight is asked of the GM too (its button is on the adventure page, between fights). Play live's Divine Smite is still an Ask the GM spell: casting it there turns on Smite of Protection. A Stroke of Luck 20 on an attack roll counts as a Critical Hit. A Dazed creature either acts where it stands or only moves (no Bonus Action). The computer-played Hero 1 does not step away with Tactical Shift. Holy Nimbus's sunlight counts for Sunlight Sensitivity; it does not light the map for seeing.

features.name: All 339 SRD creatures
features.what: Every SRD creature fights in the simulator and in Play live: attacks, Multiattack, saving-throw actions (breath weapons, sprays) with Recharge and uses per day, attack riders, and since 27 October its spells, legendary actions and special traits (see Monster spellcasting).
features.how: Pick them in Remix Live, Import map or a region battle.
features.limits: Lair actions are not played; a save action is used from where the creature stands; spells and traits the engine cannot hold (summons, teleports, Charmed, Wall of Fire) are listed for you to rule at the start of the fight.

features.name: Measured threat
features.what: Creatures rated by simulated fights, not only by CR, so Remix can swap like for like. The batch has run (27 October): 257 SRD creatures, levels 1-8, in an open arena and a corridor sized to the creature, 5 fights each against the four test heroes. Of the rated: 637 play as their XP says, 800 harder, 573 easier (docs/development/THREAT_REPORT.md).
features.how: Used by Remix.
features.limits: Measured before creatures cast their spells and used legendary actions and traits: spellcasters and legendary creatures are rated too low until they are measured again. Creatures that only swim wait for a water arena; creatures too strong for a level 8 party aren't rated yet.

features.name: Min-max and fun builds
features.what: Two shelves in the character builder: Min-max, for optimized character sheets people share with you, and Fun builds, for characters picked for synergy and fun rather than peak power.
features.how: Characters page, Min-max or Fun builds tab: Add from a file, or on any open sheet choose Put on the shelf (with a note: who made it, why it is strong or fun). On the shelf: Open sheet, Copy to my characters (checked by the rules), Edit note, Remove, Export this shelf. Kept in this browser; other people's builds are never part of Mythastria.

features.name: Characters
features.what: Import sheets from Foundry/The Forge, D&D Beyond (JSON and PDF), Fantasy Grounds, Roll20 and Iain McEwen's Google Sheets sheet; build SRD 5.2.1 characters (levels 1-20, multiclass); print a fillable PDF sheet that imports back. Since 28 October (GM: "I don't want any of the test characters. I only want to use characters saved in the saved characters tab"): every characters tab has Delete: each saved character's card and its open sheet (it leaves the party Mythastria keeps for the table too), and each sheet on the Min-max and Fun builds shelves. Test in Play live brings your other saved characters along, not test characters. Since 28 October (GM: "there needs to be a full character sheet with collapsed menues"): Play live's character panel has a Full sheet tab beside Turn and Checks & saves: the acting character's whole saved sheet, with its fight numbers on top and every section folded until opened (Abilities and saving throws, Attacks, Skills, Spellcasting, Features and traits, Gear and more, Notes); the browser remembers which are open. An imported sheet shows the fight's own attacks, spell attack and spell slots. Since 28 October (GM: "The spells available can be a pull down menu. The spell will then display and spell slot pips will show what slots are left. If the spell can be upcast, there will be a dropdown menu for the level to cast."): on the Turn tab the spells are one dropdown (by level, "not now" when it can't be cast), the chosen spell's card shows under it (drag a one-target spell onto a creature as before), the slots show as pips per level (filled: left, hollow: spent) and a Cast at dropdown chooses the slot level when the spell can use a higher one. Since 28 October (GM: "casting bless didn't do anything"): a spell for up to N creatures (Bless, Bane, Magic Missile) drags onto a creature too; each drop or click adds one, it is cast when all are picked, and Cast sends it with fewer. Since 28 October (GM: "every spell with a range or area should show that shape before selecting targets"; "lit up is better"): choosing a spell in the dropdown, or holding or casting it, lights up its reach on the map around the caster in the spell's colour, labelled (Bless: range 30 ft; Burning Hands: 15-ft Cone; Fireball: range 150 ft, 20-ft-radius Sphere); the area follows the pointer once the card is clicked; Esc or any other choice clears it. Since 28 October (GM: "also many spells like bless can be upcast"): Cast at also covers Bless (one more creature for each level above 1), Cure Wounds (+2d8), Healing Word (+2d4), Guiding Bolt, Burning Hands and Fireball (+1d6), Cone of Cold, Spiritual Weapon and Spirit Guardians (+1d8); the chosen slot is the one spent. Not yet: Hold Person and Hold Monster's extra creatures.
features.how: Characters: Import, or Build; then Test in Play live. On Play live: the Full sheet tab on the character's panel; click a section's title to open it.

features.name: Starting equipment: kit or gold
features.what: A level 1 character takes its class's SRD 5.2.1 Starting Equipment (kit A, or A or B for the Fighter) or the class's gold, and its background's equipment or 50 GP. A kit puts its armour, shield, weapons and focus on the sheet, lists its pack and other gear (Javelin ×8, Dungeoneer's Pack...), and brings its own coins; anything else picked is bought from the gold, and the builder shows what is left and why.
features.how: Characters: Build a character, step 5 Equipment: choose the class kit or gold, then the background kit or gold.
features.limits: Level 1 only (higher levels start with the GM's equipment). Packs are listed by name, not unpacked.

features.name: Photos on tokens
features.what: A character's photo becomes its token, in 2D and 3D.
features.how: Attach a saved sheet with a photo to a party token.

features.name: Players join from their own screen
features.what: Players join from their own phones or computers, anywhere, at your table's own address (a tunnel to your PC; nothing to set up on your router): they ask with your invite code, you let them in. The door limits visitors, blocks repeated wrong codes, logs who comes in, and refuses every GM control. Every screen shows each spell's effect as it is cast, whoever casts it, and your Play live screen follows a player's turn on their phone as it happens. Before joining, a player accepts a notice covering privacy, age, terms of use and the table rules.
features.how: Leave the PC on with Mythastria running. Play live, GM tools, Players... (the invite link)
features.limits: Restarting Mythastria closes the door: open it again and players ask again. (On their own screen, the player client, a seated player plays their whole turn: see "A seated player's own sheet".)

features.name: Thick walls
features.what: Walls are at least a full 5-ft square, drawn as stone blocks, with stone fading past the map's edge.
features.how: Every map follows it; imported maps too.

features.name: Import a map
features.what: Bring in a Universal VTT map (.dd2vtt, .uvtt) or a plain picture: align the grid to printed squares or survey it, paint floor, wall and door squares.
features.how: Play live, More, Import map. The map's licence is yours to respect.

features.name: Terrain battle maps
features.what: A standard outdoor battle map for any terrain: trees and boulders that block, pools and the sea, the ground's colour; it matches its region hex (a road, a river with a ford, the sea's side) and your layout (open, normal, dense; small, normal, large).
features.how: Region map: an encounter pops it up, or Battle here...; it opens in Play live.

features.name: Indoor maps and dungeons from your preferences
features.what: The sites on a made region (dungeons, caves, ruins, lairs) drawn as indoor battle maps from your design preferences: kind, size (4-15 rooms), 1-3 levels, layout (linear, branching, looping), walls (cut stone, natural cave, mixed), doors (few, some, many) and a theme in your own words. The local model in LM Studio designs the rooms (purpose, size, shape, features, a short description each) and how they join (doors, locked doors, archways, stairs); Mythastria lays them out and checks every level: walls a whole square thick with stone fading past the edge, doors in walls, passages a square or wider, every room reachable. Each room's description is a GM note on the map; braziers, hearths and lanterns light their rooms; pools are water. If the model gives nothing usable, it says so and nothing is made: no scripted map.
features.how: Region map: click a site (a red place), Draw this site as indoor maps..., choose, Draw it (a minute or two; LM Studio must be running with google/gemma-4-12b-qat). Level 1 opens in Play live and the place leads to it; every level is in Play live's map list under Region sites, then the project and the region. Another map number gives another design. What Mythastria had to change in the model's design (a room with no way in gets a passage) is said in the status line.

features.name: Region map
features.what: A 2D hex map of the region: 1-mile hexes dotted, 6-mile dashed, 24-mile solid, over a picture; terrain, numbered places you name yourself (click a place on the map), fog the party clears, and a players' view. Reset... puts the map back to its original design (as it was made, imported or first opened): places, terrain and the grid; the party is taken off the map, the fog closes and its travels are cleared.
features.how: Region map: Load picture and align the grid, or Make a region.... Every control sits on the map's frame and the page fits the window with no scrolling: Maps and Region along the top, Hex grid and Terrain and fog on the left, Party, Places and the journey log on the right. Map tools (Add a place, Place the party, Travel to..., painting) say in the bar under the map what to click; Esc puts a tool down. Clear... starts an empty region map and offers to save a copy first (Import brings it back). Reset... (beside Clear...) asks first, then puts the original design back; place the party again to begin.

features.name: Make a region from your preferences
features.what: Mythastria draws a region for you: size, climate, coast or islands, how rugged, wooded and wet; settlements joined by roads, rivers, and sites for adventures, all numbered for you to name. The same choices and number give the same region.
features.how: Region map, Make a region..., then Make it. Painting a hex afterwards repaints the picture.

features.name: Maps: projects and connected maps
features.what: Every map is kept in Mythastria on your PC, filed in a project or in Spare maps. A place can lead to another map or to a tactical map; Back returns. A whole project exports as one file and imports again with its links.
features.how: Region map, Maps panel: Project (New project..., Rename..., Delete project... moves its maps to Spare maps), its maps (Open, Delete...), File this map in, Export project / Import project. Click a place, choose Leads to, then Places: Open map. On an empty map a place leads to, Make a region, Import or Load picture fill that map, keeping its link.

features.name: Portals
features.what: A spot on a map that jumps to another map in Maps: click it to go there; when the party travels onto it, Step through takes the party along at the same day and hour. Two-way portals have a portal back where they come out.
features.how: Click a hex (Add a place) or a place, choose Kind: A portal, pick where it jumps to; for two-way, click where it comes out on that map (Esc leaves it one-way).

features.name: Travel, fast travel and encounters
features.what: Travel by SRD 5.2.1 pace (4, 3 or 2 mph), no faster than the terrain's maximum pace (Travel Terrain: plains and roads Fast; forest, hills, coast and desert Normal; mountains and swamp Slow), in 8-hour days (or push on: Extended Travel), an encounter check every 4 hours with its distance by terrain; fast travel through places you have been, with no encounters. Each pace's effect and the weather's saves: see Environment, contagions, fear and travel.
features.how: Place the party, Travel to..., then Travel or Fast travel. Pace and Weather and the march (the region's cold, heat, wind, rain, high altitude; Push on past 8 hours) are beside them.

features.name: Remix Prep
features.what: Make a played adventure fresh for a replay: swap encounters for creatures of the same measured difficulty, proved in the background, saved as a layer that never changes the original. Mounts (Camel, the horses, Mule, Pony, Mastiff, Elephant) are never offered as foes: they are domestic animals (your rule, 2026-10-23). The page is laid out symmetrically: on a desktop, paired cards of equal size in two columns (Adventures and Saved remixes; Prepare a remix and The proof's party), with the proposal and the SRD traps across both; on a phone, one column in working order. Since 28 October (GM: "I don't want any of the test characters. I only want to use characters saved in the saved characters tab"): the proof (paired fights with test characters) is removed; a remix is saved as an estimate, and Check the encounters on Play an adventure tells you whether it is winnable for your saved characters.
features.how: Remix Prep: pick the adventure and an encounter, Propose, review, tick both boxes and Save for next fight. Then Check the encounters on Play an adventure.
features.limits: A full proof can be slow on some PCs; more maps need their encounter descriptions.

features.name: Portrait and Landscape layouts
features.what: A layout preset kept on this device for every page: Auto follows the screen's width; Portrait uses each page's one-column arrangement whatever the width (a screen or tablet standing upright; on a wide screen it is a centred column); Landscape keeps the wide, side-by-side arrangement even on a narrow screen. On Play live, Landscape also puts the turn sheet left of the map (Auto does when the screen is landscape and 1000 px wide or more; Portrait never).
features.how: On the splash screen, press Auto, Portrait or Landscape under Play an adventure; or change it later with the layout menu at the end of any page's header.
features.limits: It switches the pages' own width rules (600 px and wider); a page with no narrow arrangement looks the same in both.

features.name: Simulator fights
features.what: Watch the simulator play a fight turn by turn. Since 28 October (GM: "I don't want any of the test characters. I only want to use characters saved in the saved characters tab"): the party is the saved characters you tick, each at its own level; no test characters or test item kits. Since 28 October (GM: "remove test characters from simulator fights. Allow characters to be loaded"): no sample recordings fought by the test heroes; the page starts empty, and Load characters… opens the Characters page's Import (D&D Beyond PDF or JSON, Fantasy Grounds, Foundry, Roll20, a sheet) in another tab, the new character showing in Saved characters here once saved.
features.how: Simulator fights: Load characters… (or tick them in Saved characters), pick a map, press New fight, then Next turn. Open a recording plays one you saved.

features.name: A model in the chat window
features.what: The GM can load a local model from the chat window and ask it things. What you load is also the model the Rules monitor uses.
features.how: Chat, then the Model section: choose LM Studio or Ollama, choose a model, press Load, then type a question and press Ask.
features.limits: GM only: players never see the section or the talk. Models on this PC only. The model can't see or change a fight, and the talk is gone when Mythastria restarts.

features.name: Chat and dice
features.what: Table chat on every page (share pictures, music links and sounds); a dice pool with mixed dice and a bonus (2d6 + 1d8 + 3); the dice tower, where a private roll lands blank for others.
features.how: The Chat button on every page.

features.name: Market
features.what: A market only the GM opens, with SRD 5.2.1 goods; players see a Market button while it is open.
features.how: Play live, GM tools, Market...

features.name: Party loot
features.what: The party's loot inventory: everything the party found, coins and items. Mythastria adds up the coins (PP, GP, EP, SP, CP, by the SRD 5.2.1 coin values) and divides them among the characters who share; one button pays each share into their purses. Items go into one character's bag. The players see the list and their share, read only.
features.how: Play live, GM tools, Market..., Party loot: type what the party found (one find per line: 1,200 gp, 35 sp, 40 silver pieces, Rope, Hempen (50 feet)), Add to the party loot. Tick who shares, then Pay ... into each purse. An item: choose a character, Give. Players: the Party loot button on their screen.
features.limits: A find counts as coins only when it is nothing but coins: 'a ruby worth 50 gp' is an item, never split (sell it in a shop, then share the gold). Shares are paid in one sum per purse; what doesn't divide evenly stays in the party loot. Purses are Mythastria's own: the Characters page sheet is not changed.

features.name: Give back
features.what: The GM's appeal to everyone who plays: we have leisure time, so please give your time or money to local volunteer efforts.
features.how: Give back, at the end of the page row, for the GM and for players.
features.limits: It links to no charity, and Mythastria takes no money.

features.name: One-shot builder
features.what: Build a one-shot: a story, its locations, a map for each, and what waits there: creatures, people with attitudes, SRD traps and narrative puzzles. With a model loaded in Chat, Generate writes any story field.
features.how: One-shot on the page row. Add locations, choose maps, click a square to place things, then Save and play. It appears on Play an adventure.
features.limits: Maps come from Region map's site designer or an import, so a new map needs its own step. Remix Prep needs a written encounter description, which one-shots don't have yet; Remix Live works. Puzzles have no dice: the GM rules on the answer.

features.name: On the fly
features.what: Change the fight being played without starting it again: bring in creatures or people, each with its own Initiative and attitude, read words to the table's log, set a creature's AC for this fight (a spell cast between scenes), carry out a ruling (Heal, Stabilize, Temporary HP), or call a check in a fight. A group stealth check can be ruled by a written DC instead of Perception.
features.how: Play live, Remix, On the fly, while a fight runs. Traps stay on the trap tool in GM tools. Undo step takes any of it back.
features.limits: Moving to another map still starts a new fight.

features.name: By the SRD
features.what: One switch for the GM. Off, the table's own rulings apply: the GM rolls Perception against a Hide, and Spirit Guardians deals Radiant. On, both play as the SRD writes them: Hide is a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check whose total is the DC to find the character, and Spirit Guardians deals Necrotic for an evil caster.
features.how: Play live: By the SRD, beside Turn timer. Off to start; kept for the next fights until the service restarts. Undo step counts a flip as a step. For Spirit Guardians, set Alignment in the character builder.
features.limits: Rulings where the SRD says nothing stay either way, and the group stealth check is the same either way, since the SRD leaves its DC to the GM. A sheet with no alignment isn't evil. Imported sheets don't bring an alignment yet.

features.name: Refused by the table
features.what: A log for spotting cheaters. The rules engine rolls the dice and checks every choice, so a tampered screen can only ask for what it may not have. The table lists those refusals by player: not allowed (what the table's own screen never sends, like acting for another character or calling a GM control) and against the rules (which can be an honest mistake). A player gets Worth a look after anything not allowed, or 8 rule refusals in 10 minutes. Late clicks and other timing aren't listed.
features.how: Play live, GM tools, Players...: Refused by the table. A dot on GM tools and a ! on Players... say someone is worth a look. Open a player to see each refusal and why; Clear this list when you've looked.
features.limits: A reason to look, not proof. In memory only, shown to the GM only, gone at a restart; the table's notice says so. It sees what reaches the door, so it can't see a player looking at their own screen's data, or a screen that only sends allowed choices.

features.name: Every attack has a card
features.what: A character gets a card for every attack on their sheet, up to twenty: weapons and attack cantrips alike. Before, only the two best showed and a third cantrip fell to Ask the GM.
features.how: Play live and the player's screen: Attacks, on the character sheet.
features.limits: Twenty cards at most, beyond the Light weapon's extra attack and a Monk's Unarmed Strike. A computer-played character still chooses from its first two, and turns to the others only when the party has seen the foe ignore that damage.

features.name: Cantrips by the SRD
features.what: A cantrip cast from its card does what the SRD says. Sorcerous Burst: each 8 on a d8 rolls another d8, up to your spellcasting modifier. Ray of Frost slows, Shocking Grasp stops Opportunity Attacks, Starry Wisp outlines, and Chill Touch's healing rider goes to the GM. A cantrip takes the Magic action, so Extra Attack gives no second cast. Eldritch Blast makes a roll for each beam, at any target. Sneak Attack stays with weapons.
features.how: Cast it from its card as before.
features.limits: Burst's extra d8s are always rolled: the SRD says you can, and they only add damage.

features.name: Panic Button
features.what: One red button that stops everything at once. The rules engine holds at its next step and nothing is lost; the Rules monitor and the turn timer stop; the players' choices, rolls, chat and requests are refused, and their table screen says The GM has stopped the game. The GM's own chat and Undo step still work.
features.how: Play live: Panic, on the bar beside Start live fight. It becomes Resume, which goes on from exactly there. A fight you had frozen before stays frozen.
features.limits: A pause, not a shutdown: the service keeps running and the players stay seated. The cover is on the table screen; on The Stage the buttons are refused instead. No new fight starts until Resume.

features.name: Undo step
features.what: The GM can go back through a fight one step at a time, right to its start, with no limit. A step is one choice by a player or the GM, a Reaction answered, or one creature's turn. The fight then waits, frozen, and the same choices give the same dice.
features.how: Play live: Undo step (n); hover it to see what it takes back. Press it as often as you like, then Go on.
features.limits: This fight only: a new fight starts a new count. The rules engine rebuilds the fight and plays it again up to that step, so a long fight takes a little longer, and the adventure day and the bags go back to the fight's start and are spent again: anything the market did during the fight goes back too. After the fight's end it asks first, as a rest taken since goes back as well. Chat and free dice rolls are not taken back. There is no redo; a GM choice made in the instant creatures were acting can land a moment later on replay, and if a step can't be played again the undo stops there and says so.

features.name: Turn timer
features.what: A small clock on the Combat tracker shows how long this turn has run, on every screen. It waits while the fight is frozen or stopped.
features.how: Play live: the Turn timer switch beside Influence buttons, on or off at will. Kept for the next fights until the service restarts.
features.limits: It only shows the time: it never ends a turn. It counts the turns of characters played at the table, not the creatures'.

features.name: Chat: newest on top
features.what: The chat window keeps the message box at the top with the newest post right under it, so nothing needs scrolling down to read it. The talk with a loaded model runs the same way.
features.how: Chat, on any page that has it.

features.name: The Stage's symbol
features.what: The old comedy and tragedy masks, a small gold line drawing above The Stage's buttons.
features.how: The Stage: under the logo.

features.name: A player's own Flavor
features.what: A seated player can change how their own character and the creatures it summoned look (a familiar, a steed, raised undead): name, role, footnote, picture, standee, a rider, and paint. Looks only, never stats. The GM approves each change. Until then it shows on that player's screen alone, marked as pending; once approved, everyone at the table sees it, on every map; refused, the previous look comes back with no note.
features.how: Player: My Flavor... beside Hand to the GM, then Ask the GM. GM: Asked of the GM on Play live, Approve or Refuse.
features.limits: Creatures only, not attacks or spells. A creature is known as the player's once it is on the map, so a familiar has to be called first.

features.name: Flavor
features.what: Change how a creature, attack or spell looks and reads (pets, familiars, mounts, new artwork, a footnote) without changing its rules. A creature's standee in the 3D view can stand on a round base and at its true height (otherwise drawn 40% taller), and a Large or bigger creature can carry a rider (a picture on its back, on the map and in 3D; the creature still fights with its own stat block). The artwork list also offers the 20 newer token pictures (marked "newer art"): Troll, Camel, Polar Bear, Cloaker and others that have no Retro token.
features.how: Play live, GM tools, Flavor... Pick the creature; under Creature artwork, choose a picture and tick On a round base or True height (3D view); for a Large or bigger creature, choose a Rider. Players see the same standee.

features.name: Paint on the map
features.what: The GM paints on the map with a see-through brush in any colour and size, and erases it, undoes it or clears it. The paint is kept per map, sits over the map and under the tokens and the fog, and the players' window and the player clients see it only while the GM shows it. Shown paint blocks the players' vision: on their screens a creature standing on a square at least half covered by paint at See-through 0.5 or more is not shown (map, 3D view, turn order), and the paint covers traps, hazards and notes; the party's own characters still show, and the GM's screen shows everything. The rules never read it: a character can still target what it sees by the rules. The 3D view hides those creatures but does not draw the paint itself.
features.how: Play live, GM tools, Paint. Choose Brush or Eraser, the colour, size and see-through, then drag on the map; tick Show to players to reveal it, untick to hide it. Press Paint again to go back to play.

features.name: The Stage
features.what: The role-play stage with the GM as Director: the spotlight, the Dialogue light and applause. GM 2026-10-28 ("the client side also needs The Stage"): on the player client too: a seated player opens it from The Stage link at the top of their screen and plays their own seat (join or leave the Stage, applaud, Dialogue when they hold the spotlight); the seat picker and the Director controls stay on the GM's PC.
features.how: The Stage page; players: The Stage at the top of the player client.

features.name: Skins and the miniature look
features.what: The Gilded skin for the pages (others to choose from), cartoon spell and hit effects, and the miniature-diorama 3D look; tokens keep their own colours.
features.how: Gilded is the default; a chosen skin is used on every page.

features.name: Mythastria style guide
features.what: How Mythastria reads and looks, written down from what the table already does: words (SRD 5.2.1's rules terms, plain words, refusals that say why, buttons that name what they do), screens (the Gilded look, colours by name so every skin works, contrast, the focus ring, 44 px buttons, nothing chosen for anyone) and art (style 1 cartoon, tokens never recoloured, flat standees, thick walls). It ends with a checklist for anything new and the professional guides it draws on (WCAG 2.2, the Xbox and Game Accessibility Guidelines, the RPG writing guides).
features.how: Documents, More: Mythastria style guide.
features.limits: A contrast check on 28 October found fixes, all made the same day: Parchment's green, red, amber and grey text is readable now, the edges of boxes you type in are clear in every skin, the gold focus ring shows everywhere the keyboard reaches, and no text is smaller than 11 px (the old Training table page, the Documents tags). Saying GM instead of GM everywhere is proposed for you to decide.

features.name: Monster spellcasting, legendary actions, special traits
features.what: The rest of the SRD creatures' stat blocks played by the engine and checked by the referee: Spellcasting (a Mage's Fireball and Shield, a dragon's Command and Scorching Ray: attacks, saves in Spheres, Cones, Lines and Emanations, healing, Magic Missile, Bless, uses per day, Concentration with its save after damage); legendary actions right after other creatures' turns and Legendary Resistance; traits such as Pack Tactics, Magic Resistance, Regeneration (stopped by fire or acid), Undead Fortitude, Flyby, Sunlight Sensitivity, Death Burst and Stench-like auras. Since 27 October also their lasting areas (Entangle, Moonbeam, Insect Plague, Spirit Guardians) and Haste's extra action; a creature whose Spellcasting gives no save DC (the Priest) uses 8 + its Proficiency Bonus + its spellcasting modifier.
features.how: Nothing to do: the creatures use them on their turns in Play live, Remix and the simulator, and the log says what they cast. At the start of a fight the log lists what is yours to rule ("The GM rules ...").
features.limits: Lair actions are not played. Spells with no effect in a fight, summons, teleports, Charmed and Wall of Fire cast by creatures stay with you.

features.name: Homebrew tool
features.what: Make your own creatures, spells, items and rules variants in the 2024 rules' building blocks; kept on your PC, never shared or used to train the engine.

features.name: Content packs
features.what: Import rules and art from third-party partners, at the user's own responsibility, converted into the engine's building blocks.

features.name: Rising water
features.what: Traps and events that flood rooms and caverns in stages.

features.name: Light sources in play
features.what: Torches, Hooded and Bullseye Lanterns, Lamps and Candles from a character's bag, and the Light, Continual Flame and Daylight spells, work in a live fight by SRD 5.2.1. A Torch gives Bright Light 20 ft and Dim Light 20 ft more and burns 1 hour; it is also a weapon (1 Fire damage). A Hooded Lantern gives 30/30 and its hood lowered Dim Light in 5 ft; a Bullseye Lantern a 60-ft Cone of Bright Light and Dim Light 60 ft more; a Lamp 15/30; a Candle 5/5. Lamps and Lanterns burn a flask of Oil for 6 hours. The light follows whoever holds it, and every sight rule uses it: what each character sees, the party's fog and each player's map, attacks against a creature you can't see, Darkvision (Dim counts as Bright, Darkness as Dim within range), and the creatures the game plays, which go for the enemies they can see. Dim Light gives Disadvantage on Perception by sight (passive -5, and on a Search); in Darkness a creature can't find anyone by sight. Magical Darkness lets no ordinary light in and dispels Light and Continual Flame where they overlap; Daylight is sunlight and dispels a Darkness it overlaps. A character who drops to 0 Hit Points drops their light where they fall. Lights still burning when the fight ends keep burning on the adventure day's clock: a Torch burns out, a Lantern runs out of Oil. Since 27 October a creature the game plays holds the torch or lantern its scenario gives it: the light follows it and falls where it drops at 0 Hit Points. Continual Flame's Ruby Dust (50 GP) is sold by the Market's scribe. Your rulings (27 October): dousing any light or covering a magical light is the free object interaction (only a spell's own text limits it: Continual Flame is covered, not quenched; Daylight can't be); lighting from another flame takes an action, aiming a Bullseye Lantern is free, filling a Lamp or Lantern is the Utilize action and one from the bag is empty until filled.
features.how: Play live, your turn, the sheet's Light row: Light a Torch (a Bonus Action with a Tinderbox in the bag, otherwise an action from a flame within 5 ft), Douse it, Drop it (no action: it lights the square it lies on), Hand it to an ally within 5 ft or Pick it up (the free object interaction), Lower or Raise the hood (a Bonus Action), Aim the Bullseye Lantern (click a square), Take out a Lantern and Fill it with Oil (the Utilize action). Light spells on the sheet's spell list are cast from the same row, on something you hold or on a square. Holding a lit Torch adds a Torch attack card. GM: Map light (Bright, Dim, Dark) in the view bar sets the map's own light for the running fight or the next one. On the map you see every light's rings (Bright solid, Dim dashed) and the dark veil; each player's window shows only the lights their party can see.
features.limits: Not yet: a free-hand count (holding a torch and a shield and a weapon is not checked), lights in the 3D view, lighting or dousing a light between fights on the adventure page (the service can do it; no buttons yet), monsters lighting, dousing or handing over lights, covering a light with a cloak.

features.name: Realistic 3D and lighting
features.what: A realistic renderer and real-time lighting beside the miniature look, which stays the default.

features.name: System requirements
features.what: Recommended minimum PC requirements, published with the full release.

features.name: Turn hints for players
features.what: Opt-in: hints are off until a player turns them on for their own screen. Reminders work now, straight from the rules engine and only when they are true: one quiet line by End turn (your Action is still unused, Bonus Action free with what it could be, feet of movement left, a levelled spell already cast this turn, Second Wind, Rage or Lay On Hands still usable) and a gold warning on a Concentration spell's card ("Casting Shield of Faith ends your Bless."). They name what is possible, never which to take. Only the player whose turn it is sees them; never the chat, the log or the other players. Since 28 October the GM has the last word (step H3): in Players... each seat shows its hint level, with a limit (Player chooses / Off) and a cap for the whole table (Players choose / Off for everyone). Either one lowers hints at once; neither ever turns them on: only the player does, within both. Off for everyone also turns off the hints on your own Play live screen. Since 29 October, facts while you point (your answers: no chance to hit, only Advantage or Disadvantage and why): hold an attack over a creature for "Disadvantage: an enemy within 5 ft." or "Advantage and Disadvantage cancel (...): a plain roll.", worked out by the attack's own checks without rolling, never the creature's Armor Class; a Rogue also sees "Sneak Attack applies: an ally is beside it." and, by End turn, "Sneak Attack not used this turn."; point at a square to move to for "In reach of: Goblin Warrior 1 (5 ft)." and "Goblin Warrior 3 may make an Opportunity Attack on this path (Disengage prevents it)." (the route the move really takes; hostile creatures only, none after Disengage); aim an area spell for "Inside: Goblin Warrior 1, Goblin Warrior 2 (foes); Hero 2 (ally)." (the cast's own area, and who Sculpt Spells spares). A creature the player doesn't see is never named. The sheet (and the join page) says once that hints are off and where to turn them on.
features.how: On a phone: the Hints switch above the map (Off / Reminders); the choice stays with the seat and in that browser. On your Play live screen: the Hints switch under each character's name on the sheet, Off for each character until you turn it on (hotseat). Tap the small x after a reminder to mute that kind; Mute... (Muted) brings it back. GM: Players..., "Turn hints at this table" and each seat's limit; a player's switch then shows the levels above the limit greyed out ("the GM has turned hints off"). The facts show on the line under the reminders while you hold an attack over a token, point at a square, or aim a spell; each kind mutes like a reminder.
features.limits: Off for everyone until each player turns it on (your rule). The cap and the limits are kept until Mythastria restarts (as the seats are). No "End anyway?" check: only the reminder line (your answer, 29 October). Suggestions ("What would you do?") not now (your answer). Opportunity Attacks are named only on the squares a move reaches without a Dash; area spells aimed at several points (Meteor Swarm, Fire Storm) and the spells with their own zones or summons say nothing yet.

features.name: Local-model playtester
features.what: A local model on your PC (LM Studio) takes a test seat at the players' door like a player and plays one character through whole fights, in batches, overnight too. It sees only what that seat sees, chooses one of the options the seat's screen offers (attacks, spells, actions, items, doors, moves, End turn) and the rules engine checks every choice as it does for a person; the rest of the party plays by the simulator. After each fight it writes a plain report: what the character tried and what happened, anything the screen offered that the table then refused (and why), what the model said was unclear, replies it could not use, wins, losses and unfinished fights, timings and model calls. When the model gives nothing usable three times, the fight stops there and the report says so: the playtester never plays a move in its place. Reports stay on your PC. Fun, pacing and phones still need people.
features.how: Run_Playtester.bat (LM Studio open, its server on, google/gemma-4-12b-qat loaded): Hero 2, then Hero 3, on four maps at level 2, no new fight after 8.5 hours. Or py tools\playtester.py --maps test/live_keep.json,test/goblin_den_2024.json --party Hero 2,Hero 3,Hero 1,Hero 5 --play Hero 2 --level 2. It starts its own test service on ports 8826 and 8827 and never touches your table. The report: sim\runs\playtester\<time>\REPORT.md, rewritten after every fight; every choice, with the screen the model read, in decisions.jsonl beside it.
features.limits: Fights only (no social or exploration scene), pregens only (no saved characters yet), one model seat at a time. Not offered to the model yet (the report counts them): Ask the GM (nobody rules in a test), Search or Study a square, traps and locks, mounts, Font of Magic, Metamagic, Undo. Moves are next to or toward a creature it sees, or away from the foes, not any square. Area spells are aimed at a creature's square. Foes' Hit Points are given in words (unhurt, hurt, Bloodied). The model is a first reader, not a rules expert: weigh its 'unclear' notes, and keep testing with people.

features.name: Adventures as social, exploration and combat; attitude and morale
features.what: An encounter is a scene of the three pillars: social, exploration, combat. On Play an adventure each place starts as Talk (a social scene on The Stage), Explore (the map) or Fight here; Play live has the same choice beside Start live fight. In a social or exploration scene there are no turns and no initiative: each character acts when its player chooses (the scene's focus moves to it), with a fresh Action and movement after each choice, so the party moves freely, Searches, Studies, opens doors and uses gear; fog of war, light, hazards and traps keep working. On The Stage the creatures present show their attitude (SRD: Friendly, Indifferent, Hostile); players use the Influence buttons (each takes the Action and comes to the GM to rule; the GM can turn them off) and any other ability check, and the GM rules each; every attitude change is logged with its reason. The scene changes as you play: when a Hostile creature meets the party (exploration) or talk breaks down (social), or a player tries an attack or a harmful spell, the engine offers the GM the fight and suggests who is surprised; Initiative is rolled then (d20 + Dexterity; a surprised combatant has Disadvantage, SRD 5.2.1). A fight de-escalates with the tools already built: Call a truce (back to talk), The party retreats (back to exploring), a surrender or flight (back to talk), the party's win (back to exploring); End the scene ends the encounter. Attitudes and morale: each creature's attitude comes from your prep for its group, the adventure's text, the encounter's or level's default, the map as written, or its nature; Indifferent and Friendly creatures stay out of a fight until provoked (an attack, a harmful spell, a Grapple, a Shove or damage turns it and its group Hostile); the GM rules what Influence does. Morale is prepped beside it (fights to the end, or flees, surrenders or bargains below half or a quarter of its Hit Points, when its leader is out, or outnumbered); the engine suggests, you decide.
features.how: Play an adventure: press Talk, Explore or Fight here on a place (or choose "as a social scene" or "as exploration" beside Start live fight on Play live). The scene panel on Play live (and The Scene on The Stage) shows the scene, who acts (press a character to step forward), an ability check for that character, and for the GM the engine's cards (tick who is surprised, then Start the fight, or Not yet), Talk (The Stage), Explore (the map) and Start a fight…. On The Stage the GM seat has the attitude controls; any seat can choose who urges whom, how and what, then Ask the GM. In a fight, end it from Attitudes and morale: Call a truce, The party retreats or End the scene. Remix Prep, Attitudes and morale: choose the map and party level, set each group's attitude and morale (when it breaks; its leader) and the defaults for each level or this encounter; Save; in Play live keep Saved Remix Prep ticked. Players see the attitudes of the creatures their characters see, never your prep, the morale suggestions or the scene's cards.
features.limits: The GM always starts the fight: the engine suggests it, never starts one by itself. In a scene an attack, a Grapple, a Shove or a spell that is not purely helpful (or a utility such as Light, Detect Magic, Knock) is refused and offered to the GM as the fight's start; Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Ready and Undo are for fights. A move in a scene goes up to the character's Speed each time (move again for more). Creatures' blocks here carry no Dexterity, so their Initiative is d20 + 0 (the log says so); a fight started without a scene (Simulator fights, old links) keeps the map's fixed order. A fight still stops after its rounds (10 in Play live) and the scene goes on. Remix Prep keys a group by creature kind on one map; An adventure's own attitudes are proposed in the plan, not written into the adventure. The pregens carry no Charisma score, so their Influence counts Charisma 10.

features.name: Prerequisites checked, with links
features.what: Every tool, consumable and process is offered only when its SRD prerequisites are met (proficiency, the item in the bag, gold, time, a prepared spell, the action); otherwise it says why and links to the place that fixes it (Characters, Market, Downtime). One check does it for every part of the game: the item in the bag, the Action or Bonus Action free, a skill or tool proficiency (on the sheet in any spelling, or from the class: a Druid's Herbalism Kit, a Rogue's Thieves' Tools), the gold in the purse, a spell on the sheet, days of work (Downtime). Every SRD 5.2.1 tool in a character's bag (the 17 Artisan's Tools, the kits, gaming sets and instruments) offers its Utilize uses in Play live: the tool's ability check against the use's DC, with the Proficiency Bonus only when proficient with the tool and Advantage when the skill used with it is proficient too (SRD 5.2.1 Tool Proficiency); the GM rules what a success tells. Plan: docs/development/SRD_GAPS_PLAN.md (rules engine).
features.how: Play live, on your turn: the Bag row shows each use; one that can't be made now is greyed with its reason, and → Market or → Characters opens the place that fixes it. The sheet's Checks & saves tab lists the tools you are proficient with (●) or carry, each rolled in the dice tower. A → Market link on another page opens Play live with the Market. Play an adventure: Downtime lists every need of a project the same way, met or not, with its link.
features.limits: Which skill pairs with a tool for Advantage is the GM's call; only Thieves' Tools have one here (Sleight of Hand, as the SRD's Lock says). A Bard's or Monk's chosen tools count when they are on the saved sheet.

features.name: Poisons, kits and gear in a fight
features.what: From the character's Market bag in Play live: Basic Poison and the SRD's injury and inhaled poisons (Serpent Venom, Wyvern Poison, Malice ...), Potions of Healing for yourself or an ally beside you, a Healer's Kit (the Utilize action), Antitoxin. Thrown gear, each one attack of the Attack action against a Dexterity save (DC 8 + Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus): Acid (2d6 Acid), Alchemist's Fire (1d4 Fire, then Burning: 1d4 Fire at the start of each of its turns until the fire is put out), Holy Water (2d8 Radiant to a Fiend or Undead), Oil (covered for a minute: Fire damage before it dries adds 5 Fire), a Net (Restrained until it escapes: an action and DC 10 Strength (Athletics), by it or a creature beside it; Huge or larger shrug it off). A burning character rolls on the ground (an action, then Prone), or anyone beside it douses it with a Waterskin. Thieves' Tools disarm the traps the party has found and pick locked doors (see Traps), and every other tool offers its Utilize checks. The Study and Influence actions. Each is offered only when you have it and can use it now; otherwise it says why, with a link to the Market. The computer-played heroes drink their potions and use Basic Poison too. Since 27 October a burning creature the game plays takes its 1d4 Fire at the start of its turn too, and rolls the fire out (Prone; that is its turn) at half its Hit Points or fewer, as the computer-played heroes do.
features.how: Play live, on your turn: the Bag line and the item buttons under Other actions (Throw Oil at ..., Douse the fire on ...); Put out the fire (roll on the ground) with the actions while you burn; Disarm with Thieves' Tools beside a found trap, Pick the lock beside a locked door; Study and Influence with the other actions (then click a creature).
features.limits: Oil on a creature catches from the fire Play live deals (fire weapons and cantrips such as Fire Bolt, Alchemist's Fire, fire spells, Burning), not yet from a creature's own fire attack. A Net can't be cut or attacked yet (AC 10, 5 HP); thrown gear hits creatures, not objects. The computer-played heroes don't throw gear. A Waterskin douses once per fight (it is empty after).

features.name: Traps
features.what: The eight SRD 5.2.1 traps (Collapsing Roof, Falling Net, Fire-Casting Statue, Hidden Pit, Poisoned Darts, Poisoned Needle, Rolling Stone, Spiked Pit), Nuisance or Deadly, scaled to the party's level band. The GM places them in Play live (GM tools, Traps) or an adventure pack lists them on its map; the players see one only once they find it or it goes off. A creature moving onto one sets it off (saves, damage, falls, the Net, the flame cone, the rolling stone), checked by the referee. Search or Study a square finds them (Hidden Pit: DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation)); each is made safe its own way (an Iron Spike, cutting a trip wire, plugging the holes, defacing the glyph, Thieves' Tools), only when you have the tool and can use it now, otherwise with the reason and a link to the Market. Caltrops, Ball Bearings, Oil on the ground and a Hunting Trap from your bag. Remix Prep lists the traps for the party's level. The creatures know their own lair's traps: they step round the lids and plates and over the trip wires, or wait behind a hidden one so the party walks onto it; intruders don't know them. A wary creature (a Scout, one marked wary, or one a trap hurt) Searches or Studies the floor ahead of it and finds traps by the same DCs; what it finds its side knows, never the players. Out of a pit: a Climb Speed climbs; any other way up goes to Ask the GM, who can let the character climb out; creatures climb out the same way.
features.how: Play live: GM tools, Traps: choose a trap and its levels, click a square (the statue and the stone: a second click). On your turn: Search a square or Study a square under Actions, then click the square; a found trap's buttons (Wedge an Iron Spike, Cut the trip wire ...) appear with the actions; area gear under Bag. Remix Prep: SRD traps for this level. Who knows a trap: GM tools, Traps, tick The whole lair or the creatures under the trap (an adventure pack: known_by on the trap, or knows_traps on a creature); the log shows the GM what they know and find (GM only). In a pit: Climb out of the pit; an ally beside the pit: Help ... climb out.
features.limits: In the simulator a creature's Search, or its climb out of a pit, takes its whole turn; a creature waits behind a hidden trap two turns at most; creatures of every side share what they find; the map is flat, so melee across a pit's depth is refused only in Play live; the Net and the Rolling Stone can't be attacked; Detect Magic, Knock and Arcane Lock are not offered (Ask the GM); Passive Perception finds no trap by itself: the GM decides; a computer-played creature still rolls a DC 15 climbing check.

features.name: Short and Long Rests, the adventure day
features.what: The party's day on the adventure home page: the clock, each character's Hit Points, Hit Point Dice, spell slots, uses (Second Wind, Rage, Channel Divinity, Lay On Hands, Sorcery Points ...) and Exhaustion, kept from one fight to the next on the adventure's maps. Short Rest (1 hour): spend Hit Point Dice one at a time; Pact Magic slots, one Second Wind, Rage or Channel Divinity, Action Surge, Arcane Recovery and Sorcerous Restoration come back by the SRD. Long Rest (8 hours, 16 hours apart): everything back, one Exhaustion level less. A rest is offered only when it can be taken; otherwise it says why, with a link. The rest goes on hour by hour, each hour's hazards in order (the exposure saves while resting unsheltered). An Elf (Trance) finishes a Long Rest in 4 hours and keeps watch while the others rest on. Interruptions are each character's own, and the day sees them: damage (hazard damage, mental stress), a spell other than a cantrip cast on the day, an hour or more of walking or toil, Initiative for the fight they are in; the Short Rest is lost for that character, the Long Rest takes it 1 more hour. A character at 0 Hit Points after a fight, a hazard or travel keeps making death saves (one at a time on the page, or as time passes) until stable, healed or dead; a DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check, a Healer's Kit or Spare the Dying stabilizes it, and a stable one regains 1 Hit Point after 1d4 hours. Potions and healing spells heal on the day. Tireless (Ranger 10) and Natural Recovery (Druid 6) on a Short Rest.
features.how: Play an adventure: start the adventure and choose the party; The party's day shows Short Rest and Long Rest. During a Short Rest press Spend a d8 (or d10 ...) for each Hit Point Die, then Finish. A fight from Fight here starts from the day and writes it back; End the fight stops a fight that is going nowhere. During a Long Rest: Rest 1 hour (or Finish); each card shows when that character's rest ends, or that it is done and keeps watch. On a card: Cast a spell…, Hazard damage…, and while resting Walked or toiled…. A dying card: Roll a death save; for each conscious ally Medicine, Healer's Kit (from the bag) or Spare the Dying; Give a potion or Heal (GM).
features.limits: Spells cast on the day are entered by hand (name, slot level, healing dice); their other effects are the GM's. Hazard damage is the GM's dice (a fall, burning ...): the SRD's hourly exposure gives Exhaustion, not damage, so it does not interrupt a rest. Travel on the region map is refused while a rest is under way (stop it first). The 16 hours between Long Rests count from the party's last end, not an Elf's earlier one. Spare the Dying is offered only when the sheet lists it (the pregens don't).

features.name: End the adventure: keep playing, freeze the fight, or stop it and unload
features.what: End the adventure asks first. With a fight running the GM chooses: Keep playing; Freeze the fight (nothing moves: the creatures wait at their next step and every combat button on Play live is greyed until the GM unfreezes it); or Stop the fight and unload (the characters keep what they have left and the adventure's maps leave Play live). Without a fight it asks once more before unloading. Saved remixes and notes stay.
features.how: Play an adventure: Tonight, End the adventure (unload it), then choose. On Play live the GM's Freeze / Unfreeze button sits beside End turn; a frozen fight shows a gold banner on every screen.
features.limits: A creature already in the middle of a step finishes that step before it waits.

features.name: Crafting, brewing and scribing
features.what: Downtime by the SRD 5.2.1, between adventures, beside the party's day. Craft a nonmagical item: the tool its Craft line names, carried and with proficiency; raw materials worth half its price; its price in GP / 10 days. Brew a Potion of Healing: the Herbalism Kit, 25 GP, 1 day. Scribe a Spell Scroll of a spell on the sheet: Arcana or Calligrapher's Supplies; the Spell Scroll Costs table; a costly Material component at hand; the scroll keeps the scribe's spell save DC and attack. Craft a magic item: Arcana and the Magic Item Tools table's tool; the rarity's days and gold (halved for a consumable), plus the weapon or armor it is made from; raw materials found 75 percent of the time in a city and 25 in another settlement (rolled for all to see), else look again 7 days later. One assistant with the same proficiency divides the time (the GM may allow more). Every prerequisite is checked first; a missing one says why, with a link to Characters or the Market. The gold comes from the Market purse and the finished item goes into the bag. Each character makes one thing at a time.
features.how: Play an adventure: start the adventure and choose the party; under Downtime choose who, what and the item or spell, tick what the GM rules (materials available, the item's spells prepared, more assistants), then Start the project when every check is green. Downtime days pass: each day is 8 hours of work on every project and a Long Rest; a finished item is in the character's Market bag.
features.limits: The GM rules whether a nonmagical item's raw materials are available and checks the spells a magic item casts (the list doesn't name them); the GM assigns a tool to an item the SRD lists none for (a Shield, Holy Water, the packs). Spell Scrolls from the bag can't be read in Play live yet. Days pass on the loaded adventure's clock. Not built: other downtime (training, research, selling at a profit).

features.name: Environment, contagions, fear and travel
features.what: The SRD 5.2.1 hazards, played by Mythastria. On the adventure day, as time passes, rests and travel: Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat (its DC climbs each hour; Medium or Heavy armor has Disadvantage; drinkable water spares you) and swimming in deep water ask a Constitution save at the end of each hour of exposure; food and water are checked at each day's end (Dehydration, Malnutrition). Exhaustion is kept from fight to fight and a Long Rest removes one level (not one a contagion, thirst or hunger still holds). Cackle Fever, Sewer Plague and Sight Rot: the GM exposes a character (its save) or infects one; 1d4 days before the effects begin; Sewer Plague's save each dawn, half Hit Points from Hit Point Dice and no Long Rest recovery; Cackle Fever's held level, its three Long Rest saves and its laughter in fights; Sight Rot's blindness, the ointment and Heal or Lesser Restoration. Mental stress (a Wisdom, Intelligence or Charisma save, Psychic damage, a short-term, long-term or indefinite effect) on the day or in a fight; fear (Frightened of its source, a Wisdom save at the end of each turn) in a fight. In Play live: slippery ice (Difficult Terrain, DC 10 Dexterity save or Prone), thin ice (breaks under too much weight into frigid water), frigid water (minutes equal to the Constitution score, then a save each minute or Exhaustion), strong wind (ranged weapon attacks at Disadvantage, fliers land or fall, fog disperses, flames go out), a sandstorm and heavy rain or snow (Perception at Disadvantage); a creature can carry a contagion. On the region map: each terrain's maximum pace, each pace's effect, Extended Travel past 8 hours, High Altitude, Slower Travelers and the encounter's distance; the adventure day's clock runs with the journey. The sheet in Play live and the party's day show Exhaustion's effects, each contagion and lasting stress.
features.how: Play an adventure, The party's day: Environment, hazards and travel pace (the weather, shelter, drinkable water; Mental stress...); on each character, Exhaustion and Food, water and contagions (Expose, Infect; Heal or Lesser Restoration, Ointment..., End). Play live: GM tools, Hazards: tick the weather, click squares and Place the ice or water; Fear, mental stress and contagions for the creatures ticked (Carries it: a creature spreads one). Region map: Pace, and Weather and the march (Push on past 8 hours).
features.limits: Your readings (confirmed 27 October): dawn is 06:00; a contagion is fought (dawn and Long Rest saves) once its effects begin; Thin Ice weighs creatures by the GM's estimates by size (the SRD gives no weights). Not yet: Heavy Precipitation's Lightly Obscured for sight (only Perception's Disadvantage), the SRD's sample fear and stress tables (the GM sets the DC), Calm Emotions, Greater Restoration as a spell (the GM lowers Exhaustion), mounts' double pace for an hour, Sight Rot spread by touch (the GM exposes). The region map keeps its own travel clock; its journeys' hours are added to the adventure day. Fast travel's nights follow the day's shelter setting.
